gloss: tasting for poison; trying food first

definitions.gloss: tasting for poison; trying food first (to check it)
definitions.explanation: Originally tasting a lord's food before he ate to make sure it was not poisoned. Now used jokingly for tasting food first, for example to check whether it tastes all right.

examples.japanese: ⟦{殿様|とのさま}→殿様：10455_tonosama⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{食事|しょくじ}→食事：02087_shokuji⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{家来|けらい}→家来：12397_kerai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{毒見|どくみ}⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: A retainer tasted the lord's meals for poison.

examples.japanese: ⟦{初|はじ}めて→初めて：02932_hajimete⟧⟦{作|つく}った→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧⟦{料理|りょうり}→料理：01523_ryouri⟧な⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦{夫|おっと}→夫：00982_otto⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{毒見|どくみ}⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦もらった→もらう：00520_morau⟧。
examples.english: It was a dish I'd never made before, so I had my husband try it first.

notes:
⟦{毒|どく}→毒：10052_doku⟧ (poison) + ⟦{見|み}→見る：00283_miru⟧ (looking, checking). Also written {毒味|どくみ}.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {毒見|どくみ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ / {毒見|どくみ}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to taste for poison; to try first
- {毒見|どくみ}⟦{役|やく}→役：12557_yaku⟧: a food taster (historical); jokingly, the person who tries first

USAGE:
The modern joking use is common at home and among friends. It implies the food might be a failure, so asking a guest to {毒見|どくみ} would be rude.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{味見|あじみ}→味見：08158_ajimi⟧: tasting while cooking, to check seasoning
